title: Task graph
description: The dynamic half of the lifecycle. The declarative workflow says what must be true; this says how this particular change gets there. It is generated per work item and rebuilt when a replan happens, so no two changes are forced through an identical sequence.

generation.description: Incremented on every replan. Generation 3 means this plan is the third the organization has believed in, and history.jsonl says why the first two stopped being true.

title.description: Human-readable name, from the stage. Minimum length 1 rather than a round number: WF-DEFECT has a stage legitimately called 'Fix', and a schema that rejects it is enforcing a preference rather than a contract.

role.description: The agent responsible. Must exist in policies/agent-registry.json.

execution.description:
How this task runs, organizationally. Three values, because they answer three different questions: `declared` is what the workflow author asked for before the situation existed, `resolved` is what the resolver decided at claim time, and `actual` is what the runtime reports having done. Recording only one of them means the organization cannot tell the difference between a policy it chose, a degradation it accepted, and a spawn that ignored both.

Three modes, matching sdlc-workflow.schema.json and policies/execution-policy.json. This enum used to carry five -- `background` and `dynamic-workflow` as well -- while the workflow schema allowed only three, so a stage author could not declare either and the resolver carried a rule for `declared == "background"` that could never fire. Whether a subagent runs in the foreground or the background is a property of the runtime, not a different kind of organizational execution, and it is recorded in `runtime` below. A dynamic workflow is an orchestration mechanism, not a fourth thing a role can be.

`worktree` is not here either: where a task runs is `isolation`, a separate dimension, because a team that needs its own checkout is still a team.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for declared, before anything has been resolved.

briefing_required.description: The resolved isolation puts the spawn in its own checkout, and an isolated spawn does not receive SubagentStart's additionalContext. The task briefing has to travel in the spawn prompt instead. Kept on execution rather than on isolation because it is a fact about how the spawn must be made, which is the spawner's concern.

actual_evidence.description: The runtime event that determined `actual`. Without this, `actual` is a copy of `resolved` wearing a different name -- which is what it was: observe_subagent set actual to the resolution it had just read back, so the field proved the graph agreed with itself.

actual_undetermined.description: Why the runtime evidence could not name the mode. SubagentStart carries only agent_id and agent_type -- no teammate marker, no isolation flag -- so where teams are enabled a spawn could be either and this says so instead of guessing.

runtime.description: What the platform did with the execution, as distinct from what the organization asked for. Claude Code already decides foreground or background for a subagent based on whether the result is needed immediately, and `claude --bg` dispatches a session that outlives its caller. Neither changes the role, the accountability or the definition of done, so neither is an execution mode.

background.description: The work ran detached from the session that asked for it.

session_id.description: The platform's own id for the run, where it has one -- what `claude agents` lists and `attach` takes.

provider.description: Which execution engine ran it. Claude Code today; the field exists so the organization does not silently assume there is only ever one.

max_attempts.description: A loop without a bound is a hang. On exhaustion the task escalates rather than retrying, because the same failure three times is information about the plan, not about the attempt.

coupled_surface.description: The surface this task touches, from policies/coupling-policy.json. Two runnable tasks naming the same surface are never handed out together.

owner_agent.description: The agent_id currently holding this task, from SubagentStart. One agent holds one task and a held task is never offered again, so a result can be attributed to exactly one task rather than to every task sharing its role.

failure_class.description: The kind of the most recent failure, from policies/control-loop-policy.json.

failure_signature.description: A stable identity for the most recent failure. Compared with the previous one to tell a repeat from progress; comparing the observed wording read 'API returns 401' and 'endpoint still returns 401' as two different failures.

native_task.description: The Claude Code task this graph task is bound to, when one exists. Written at claim time so the completion gate can match on an id rather than on a substring of a subject line.

parent.description: The stage task this one was decomposed out of. The parent keeps the stage's definition of done and depends on all its children, so the stage gate the rest of the graph was promised still exists.

synthesis.description: On a parent: how it came to be decomposed.

owns_paths.description: Repository paths or globs this task will edit. Declared, not discovered -- nothing here can know what a task will touch before it touches it. What it buys is that scripts/infer_dependencies.py can then order tasks that edit the same file, or edit a file that imports another task's file.

derived_depends_on.description: Dependencies added by inference rather than by the plan, each with the evidence that produced it, so a wrong edge can be found and argued with instead of silently slowing the graph down.

isolation.description: Where this task runs: the checkout everything else is in, its own git worktree, or a remote environment. Orthogonal to execution -- subagent+worktree, background+worktree, team+shared-checkout and inline+shared-checkout are all real combinations. The same three values as execution, and for the same reason: a worktree can be resolved and not created, and `actual` has to be able to disagree.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for declared, before anything has been resolved.

actual_evidence.description: The runtime event that determined `actual` -- for a worktree, the WorktreeCreate the hook recorded. SubagentStart carries no isolation flag, so without a worktree event there is nothing to observe and `actual` stays unset rather than assumed.

actual_undetermined.description: Why the runtime could not name the isolation. This is the common case: no event says a spawn ran in the shared checkout, so shared-checkout is inferred from the absence of a worktree rather than observed, and saying so keeps the inference visible.

complexity.description: Carried from the stage so the intensity resolver can read it without re-opening the workflow. A statement about the work, not about the stage's position.

intensity.description: How much of the department cycle this task walks. Two values rather than three: `declared` is the level before the facts were applied, `resolved` is the level the signals produced. There is no `actual` -- unlike execution, nothing in the runtime reports how much review a task received, and a field nothing can observe would be a copy of `resolved` wearing a different name. What is observable is at the end: the acceptance condition fails if the verdict the level required was never recorded.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for declared, before anything has been resolved.
